english.title: Fail to provide information required by waste regulation authority / Secretary of State
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) failed, without reasonable excuse to comply with a notice served in writing by the

(A)_[the Secretary of State]_
(B)_[a waste regulation authority namely **(..SPECIFY THE AUTHORITY..)]_

requiring you to furnish such information specified in that notice namely **(..SPECIFY THE INFORMATION REQUIRED..) which the

(C)_[Secretary of State reasonably considered he needed,]_
(D)_[waste regulation authority reasonably considered it needed,]_

in the

(E)_[form specified]_
(F)_[period following service of the notice or at such time as was specified]_
(G)_[form and period following service of the notice or at such time as was specified]_
english.legislation: Contrary to section 71(3) of the Environmental Protection Act 1990.

english.notes: The power given by section 71(2) of the Environmental Protection Act 1990 has been conferred not merely for the purpose of obtaining evidence against offenders but also for the broad public purpose of protecting public health and the environment. Accordingly, persons who are required under section 71(2) to provide information cannot rely on the privilege against self-incrimination under English law or the principles under the European Convention on Human Rights for refusing to do so although the question of exclusion on the grounds of prejudice of any potentially incriminating answers may arise in any subsequent criminal proceedings - R v Hertfordshire County Council Ex parte Green Environmental Industries Limited 2000.

other.penalty:
Summary: A fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: Two years imprisonment and/or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
